s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent skin lesion with possible metastasis
salient_findings: Recurrent skin lesion on the dorsum of the right thumb
key_facts: 56-year-old man
Four-year history of skin lesion on the right thumb
Partial amputation of the thumb in December 2016
Lesion reappeared in August 2017
No significant medical history
No medications
1.8 × 1.3 cm lesion on the dorsum of the right thumb stump
Lesion is mobile over deep structures
No palpable lymphadenopathy
Metastatic workup included CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis and a bone scan
Enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node presumed to represent metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent skin lesion with possible metastasis

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive nature and potential for metastasis

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Highly aggressive skin cancer with potential for metastasis

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common skin cancer, although less likely to metastasize

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Locally aggressive skin tumor with potential for metastasis

raw.rationale: The lesion's recurrence after partial amputation and the presence of an enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node suggest an aggressive skin cancer, which is more typical of squamous cell carcinoma than other options

rejected.label: Melanoma
rejected.why: No mention of pigmentation or other characteristic features of melanoma

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically has a more rapid growth rate and is more aggressive, but the four-year history does not suggest this

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Less likely to metastasize and typically has a slower growth rate

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: Characterized by a slow-growing, painless nodule, which does not fit the aggressive nature of this case
